top.title: 2027 will test clarity of Nigeria’s legal framework on electoral justice – INEC
top.description: …warns AI, digital threats may spill into courtrooms … as 375 tribunal judges take oath By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Monday said the 2027 general elections would test not only its operational preparedness but also the effectiveness and clarity of the nation’s legal framework for electoral justice. According to the Commission, the political stability of the nation will depend not only on how efficiently it conducts elections, but equally on how courageously, transparently and justly the judiciary adjudicates the disputes that follow. The Chairman of the electoral body, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, spoke at the opening ceremony of a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the 2027 election petition tribunals held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja. The workshop was preceded by the inauguration of 375 judges who will serve on tribunals that will hear election petitions filed by aggrieved parties across the country. Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, vests in the President of the Court of Appeal the responsibility of constituting Election Petition Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes arising from National and State Houses of Assembly and Governorship elections. Similarly, Section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, prescribes the timelines for constituting the tribunals and opening their registries. Describing the workshop’s theme, “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability,” as apt, the INEC Chairman stressed that, with the general election scheduled to commence on January 16, 2027, the Commission recognises that the legitimacy of the country’s constitutional democracy rests upon impartial electoral administration and fearless judicial adjudication. He said: “While INEC manages the ballot, deploys technology, and safeguards the voter franchise, the Election Petition Tribunals stand as the ultimate guardians of democratic legitimacy. “When political contestations overflow from polling units into the courtroom, the Judiciary provides the constitutional sanctuary where grievances are transformed into peace, unlawful shortcuts are corrected, and the sovereign choice of the electorate is vindicated under the Rule of Law. “The credibility of elections cannot be measured solely by the conduct of voting or the declaration of results. It depends equally on public confidence that electoral disputes will be determined independently, fairly and in accordance with the law. “Citizens must be assured not only that their votes count, but also that the legal system is capable of protecting their democratic choices. “The consequences of electoral judgments frequently extend beyond candidates and political parties. They affect public confidence, the legitimacy of elected institutions and democratic stability. “Judicial scrutiny also provides an important mechanism of accountability for election administration. top.title: ‘He’s a coward. He can’t coach’: Dave Portnoy demands apology after being ‘right about Ryan Day from the jump’
top.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect It was a rough weekend for Michigan, as the Wolverines lost to rival Michigan State and fired their offensive coordinator. But Barstool Sports founder and devoted Michigan fan Dave Portnoy still found something to celebrate. Ohio State suffered a blowout loss of its own, falling to Oregon for its second straight defeat. And Portnoy, who has been a longtime critic of Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day, said he’s owed an apology from every Ohio State fan in Columbus. Portnoy’s Feud With Ryan Day Portnoy has been one of Day’s harshest critics for years, and things have only gotten more personal this season. In August, he called Day a “scared little chicken-boy” after Ohio State moved its senior day from the Michigan game to Week 1. Then in October, Barstool was removed from Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff , and Portnoy blamed Day for the decision. “I always knew Ryan Day was soft but holy sh*t even I didnt realize he was this soft,” Portnoy wrote on X at the time, calling the Buckeyes coach “Cryin Ryan.” Awful Announcing noted that the breakup was always inevitable . A couple of weeks later, Portnoy said that Day “would be unsuccessful at any program other than Ohio State.” “Ryan Day was born on third base,” Portnoy said. “Like, anybody here could coach that team to 10, 11 wins.” This weekend gave Portnoy plenty of new material. Michigan fell 15-6 to Michigan State, and the Wolverines fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, whom Portnoy had called “horrific.” But Ohio State blew a 14-0 lead in a 41-28 loss to Oregon, its second straight defeat, and Day said afterward that “there needs to be accountability” for the team’s struggles. ‘He’s a coward’ On Monday’s episode of Wake Up Barstool , Portnoy made it clear that he was enjoying Ohio State’s struggles. “I want an apology from every single person in Columbus. I want them to get in line and line up,” Portnoy said, in a clip shared by the show . “I want them all to come in a receiving line and say, ‘Hey, Dave Portnoy, you’ve been right about Ryan Day from the jump. He’s a coward. He can’t coach. He was born on third base.’ All of it. Get in line and say, ‘I’m sorry, you should be back on Big Noon Kickoff . It was a joke what they did to you,'” he continued. Portnoy admitted that Michigan has problems of its own, but he said that Ohio State’s situation is even worse given the talent on the roster. “Yes, we have problems in Ann Arbor, but that team’s a joke with the talent they have. So yeah, real bad weekend for Michigan, no doubt,” Portnoy said. “But let’s not forget, as bad as a weekend Michigan had, Michigan State had a worse weekend, and Ohio State had the worst weekend of the bunch.” Needless to say, Portnoy is going to enjoy every minute of this before The Game. top.title: AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars make bold move, trading for Falcons safety Jessie Bates III
top.description: Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III (3) and Xavier Watts (31) celebrate after Bates III intercepted a San Francisco 49ers' Brock Purdy pass during the second half of an NFL football game in Atlanta, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson) (Brynn Anderson/Associated Press) The Jacksonville Jaguars took a big swing a day before the NFL trade deadline , grabbing All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons on Monday morning, according to multiple reports . The Jaguars (6-2), who are just a half-game behind the Buffalo Bills and Denver Broncos for best record in the AFC and have a three-game lead over the Houston Texans in the AFC South, are giving up a second-round pick in next year's NFL draft and a fifth-rounder in 2028. By comparison, the Texans gave up a second- and seventh-rounder in exchange for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and a sixth-round pick last month. Bates, who will turn 30 years old in February, is in the final year of a four-year, $64 million contract and is still playing well. The former second-round pick out of Wake Forest, made the Pro Bowl in 2023 and was second-team All-Pro last season. Bates, who has made 61 straight starts and hasn't missed a game since 2022, also was second-team All-Pro in 2020 and 2023. "Woke up a Jaguar!," Bates posted on Twitter on Monday morning. The Jaguars had an urgent need at safety ever since former Texans defensive back Eric Murray was lost for the season due to an elbow he injury he suffered against the Colts last week. Murray, who left the Texans for a three-year, $19.5 million contract with Jacksonville following the 2024 season, had started 17 games for the Jaguars over the past two seasons before the injury. The Jaguars' defense ranks second in the league, giving up just 15.1 points per game, but they have been vulnerable through the air. Jacksonville ranks 22nd in pass defense, allowing 229 passing yards per game. When the Texans beat Jacksonville 34-31 in London last month, C.J. Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns. The Texans and Jaguars meet again on Dec. 20 at Reliant Stadium. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. top.title: Mowbray's 'soldiers and artists' march up the table
top.description: [BBC] Since the lengthy international break across September and October, Blackburn Rovers have taken 12 points from a possible 21. That is a healthy return by any measure. The only real blemish was the 4-0 hammering at Swansea City , a day on which Rovers never turned up. Beyond that, there has been plenty to like. With just over a third of the season gone, it feels like the perfect moment to take stock. Most importantly, Rovers are looking up, not down. Twelve months ago, supporters were nervously checking the bottom end of the table. Now the conversation is about the play-offs. That alone tells you how much has changed. And it's about more than points. Ewood Park feels alive again. That revival began under Michael O'Neill, but Tony Mowbray has kept the momentum going. Matchdays feel like events once more. The big away followings have helped. Not many clubs can hand over more than 7,000 tickets to travelling supporters, and fans have responded in numbers. Crowds nudging 20,000 for games against Middlesbrough, Coventry City, Leicester City and West Ham over the past seven months have brought a buzz back to the place. The only defeat among them came in a dead-rubber against an already relegated Leicester side. The positivity extends beyond the stands. Most of this squad bears the scars of last season's struggles. Apart from Sam Morsy, Jayden Fevrier and Gady Beyuku, these players have lived through difficult times at Ewood. Yet they look liberated rather than burdened by the experience. That's where the Mowbray factor comes in. His "soldiers and artists" philosophy sounds simple, but right now it's working a treat. The artists are thriving. Todd Cantwell and Dapo Afolayan have become central figures. Both have stayed fit. Both along with centre back Sean McLoughlin are ever-presents. Both are proving they can be difference-makers. That's a far cry from last season. Afolayan managed just one start after his February arrival and was hooked at half-time. Cantwell started fewer than half of Rovers' league games and never really had the freedom to express himself. This team is playing with far more adventure, which suits both players perfectly. Anyone familiar with Mowbray's career should not be surprised. For all his reputation as a no-nonsense centre-half, his teams have always tried to attack. That's in his DNA. It always has been. Then there are the soldiers. Morsy remains the heartbeat of the side. Mowbray calls him his coach on the pitch and it is easy to understand why. His influence seems to be rubbing off on academy graduate Kristi Montgomery, who looks increasingly comfortable at Championship level. Together, they give Rovers a solid foundation. The next phase of the season now feels crucial. There are 24 league matches and at least one FA Cup tie before the next international break. top.description: Cardinals' Budda Baker's stance on trade rumors revealed by NFL insider originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals lost again in Week 9, and it's very obvious that they will be sellers at the NFL trade deadline. They've already traded Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jacoby Brissett this season. So, who's next? While the running back, tight end, and wide receiver rooms seem set, the Cardinals might trade from their defense. One player worth keeping an eye on is fan favorite safety Budda Baker. While the Cardinals might not want to trade him, ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler revealed that Baker would "welcome" a trade from the Cardinals this season to a contender. Budda Baker would 'welcome' a trade from Cardinals "My sense is Budda Baker would welcome a chance to play for a contender if AZ entertains talks (big if)," Fowler reports. While Fowler isn't reporting that the Cardinals are looking to trade Baker, or that Baker has requested a trade, it does reveal a trade is much more in play than it might've been in years past. Baker isn't opposed to being traded, especially if it's to a real contender. The Buffalo Bills would be a team to watch in the sweepstakes for the star safety. Arizona is in a rebuild, and trading a veteran player for a haul of draft picks would make sense. There's no guarantee Baker will be traded, but he is at least open to a trade. top.title: Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Political economist Pat Utomi has accused the APC-led government of abandoning its responsibilities while Nigerians pay out of pocket for basic services, from electricity and water to roads, healthcare and education. In a post on his X handle on Monday, Utomi questioned what citizens receive in return for paying taxes when households and communities must fund services that government is expected to provide. “The only thing this APC-led government is good at doing is making your life worse,” he wrote. Utomi said Nigerians buy generators to cope with unreliable electricity, sink boreholes for water and contribute money to repair roads. He also cited private security, healthcare and schools as costs families increasingly bear because public institutions have been neglected. He added that waste disposal, drainage, streetlights and transformers had also become private financial responsibilities. “Then what exactly are we paying this APC-led government to do?” he asked, arguing that governments elsewhere invest public resources in education, healthcare, infrastructure and social welfare. Utomi also criticised the government’s appeals for patience and sacrifice amid economic hardship. He cited the removal of petrol subsidies and increases in electricity tariffs and university fees, alongside rising healthcare costs. “But how much more must the people sacrifice while those in power continue to enjoy the privileges of office?” he asked. Utomi argued that taxation obliges government to provide public services, describing it as more than a contribution from citizens to politicians. “The government cannot collect from the people, abandon its responsibilities and then demand applause from the people they’re making their lives difficult,” he wrote. He concluded with a challenge to the government: “If Nigerians must finance their own survival, what exactly is the purpose of government?” In a separate post on Sunday, Utomi said the APC government had made the daily struggle to earn a living an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. He described the hardship as a tragedy for a richly endowed nation that he believes is poorly governed. He said: “The incompetence of the APC government has turned the daily struggle for survival into an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. Those who labour honestly to earn a living are being punished by a system that should be making their lives easier. What a tragedy for a nation so richly endowed yet so poorly governed!” The post Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.description: …warns AI, digital threats may spill into courtrooms … as 375 tribunal judges take oath By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Monday said the 2027 general elections would test not only its operational preparedness but also the effectiveness and clarity of the nation’s legal framework for electoral justice. According to the Commission, the political stability of the nation will depend not only on how efficiently it conducts elections, but equally on how courageously, transparently and justly the judiciary adjudicates the disputes that follow. The Chairman of the electoral body, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, spoke at the opening ceremony of a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the 2027 election petition tribunals held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja. The workshop was preceded by the inauguration of 375 judges who will serve on tribunals that will hear election petitions filed by aggrieved parties across the country. Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, vests in the President of the Court of Appeal the responsibility of constituting Election Petition Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes arising from National and State Houses of Assembly and Governorship elections. Similarly, Section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, prescribes the timelines for constituting the tribunals and opening their registries. Describing the workshop’s theme, “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability,” as apt, the INEC Chairman stressed that, with the general election scheduled to commence on January 16, 2027, the Commission recognises that the legitimacy of the country’s constitutional democracy rests upon impartial electoral administration and fearless judicial adjudication. He said: “While INEC manages the ballot, deploys technology, and safeguards the voter franchise, the Election Petition Tribunals stand as the ultimate guardians of democratic legitimacy. “When political contestations overflow from polling units into the courtroom, the Judiciary provides the constitutional sanctuary where grievances are transformed into peace, unlawful shortcuts are corrected, and the sovereign choice of the electorate is vindicated under the Rule of Law. “The credibility of elections cannot be measured solely by the conduct of voting or the declaration of results. It depends equally on public confidence that electoral disputes will be determined independently, fairly and in accordance with the law. “Citizens must be assured not only that their votes count, but also that the legal system is capable of protecting their democratic choices. “The consequences of electoral judgments frequently extend beyond candidates and political parties. nigeria.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure Chieftains of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Igbara-Oke, Ifedore Local Government Area of Ondo State, have defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The defectors were received by an APC delegation led by Senator Niyi Adegbonmire, representing Ondo Central Senatorial District, and Hon. Festus Akingbaso, member of the House of Representatives, alongside other party leaders. Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Bayo Adejuwon said their decision to join the APC was motivated by what he described as the developmental strides of the ruling party in the area. Adejuwon said the APC leadership was familiar with their political influence, adding that their contributions would be reflected in the party’s performance in the 2027 elections. He said the new members were committed to working for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and the victory of other APC candidates in the state. Another defector, Faloyo, who identified himself as an indigene of Ijare, expressed satisfaction with the decision to join the APC and pledged to mobilise votes from his community for Tinubu and other party candidates in the January 16 and February 6 elections. Addressing the gathering, former Ondo State APC Chairman, Engr. Ade Adetimehin, described the defectors as the last batch of PDP members in the ward. He said their defection demonstrated the APC’s growing presence in the area and urged them to return to their respective communities to begin mobilisation ahead of the elections. Adetimehin expressed confidence in the electoral prospects of Tinubu, Adegbonmire and Akingbaso, describing the APC as an inclusive party. Also speaking, an APC leader in Ifedore, Tobi Ogunleye, said the defection was voluntary, insisting that the new members were not recruited through inducement. He alleged that some APC members in the state were working against the interests of the party’s candidates under the guise of a Rainbow Coalition, insisting that those at the gathering represented the authentic APC. Ogunleye warned that anyone working against the party’s candidates was undermining Tinubu’s transformation agenda. He also attributed the weakening of the ADC and SDP in the state to the influence of the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo. Ogunleye further claimed that the defection had effectively eliminated opposition presence in Ifedore, describing the new APC members as key figures in the opposition political structure before their decision to join the ruling party. nigeria.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences, including rape as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him. Brand, 51, showed no emotion as Judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims who had suffered significant and lasting harm. Paying tribute to the “bravery” of the women who came forward, the judge told Brand he had acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”. Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen. The woman said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004. “For many years, as his star was rising, it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court. nigeria.title: Nvidia plunges but tech shares rebound, oil prices slump
nigeria.description: Technology share prices clawed back some of last week’s sharp losses on Monday, though gains were tempered by a plunge in Nvidia following a probe into its boss Jensen Huang over claims of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oil prices fell five percent on hopes for diplomatic talks aimed at ending the US-Iran war. Chipmakers and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence boom took a hammering in the days after last Tuesday’s US midterm elections, which saw Democrats sweep both chambers of Congress, leading to speculation lawmakers would seek to rein in tech firms. But Wall Street’s main indices opened higher, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq adding 0.9 percent. Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare said the rebound in equities was due to more than just the drop in oil prices. “What we also have this morning is an inclination to buy into last week’s weakness, and specifically into the large losses seen in the AI trade,” he said in a note to clients. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which includes major chipmakers and AI firms, rose 1.9 percent. But the gains did not extend to Nvidia, which saw its shares slump more than eight percent as trading got underway in New York. O’Hare said Nvidia was being treated as a one-off story by investors for the moment. “In other words, the stock is being penalized for Jensen Huang’s personal transgression, which has invited a great deal of uncertainty into the mix, but the market isn’t caught up in the notion that this situation is going to have a systemic domino effect,” he said. The news that Nvidia’s board would investigate whether Huang had been targeted in a foreign espionage plot, following his admission he was unfaithful to his wife, brought fresh uncertainty in the markets. In a message to company employees released to media on Sunday, Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologised to his family and company staff. Alabi said Nigeria’s food security challenges could not be addressed through increased production alone without adequate infrastructure to preserve, process and distribute farm produce. nigeria.title: Mourinho wins La Liga Manager of the Month award after perfect October
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has been named La Liga Manager of the Month for October after guiding the Spanish giants to three consecutive victories, including a 2-1 El Clasico triumph over Barcelona. La Liga announced the Portuguese coach as the October winner in a post on its official X account on Monday, recognising his side’s 100 per cent winning record in the league during the month. “Real Madrid’s coach is the Coach of the Month for October in #LALIGAEASPORTS,” the post read. Mourinho’s side began the month with a 1-0 victory over Villarreal before thrashing Sevilla 4-1 and defeating Barcelona 2-1 in their first El Clasico meeting of the season. The victory over Barcelona on October 25 was particularly significant, as it handed the Catalan side their first league defeat of the campaign after winning their opening nine matches. Kylian Mbappe scored twice for Madrid, while Raphinha got Barcelona’s only goal in the encounter. Mourinho emerged ahead of Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone and Real Sociedad coach Pellegrino Matarazzo, who were also nominated for the monthly award. Simeone guided Atletico to three victories during October, beating Alaves 2-1 before recording 1-0 wins over Espanyol and Deportivo La Coruna. Matarazzo also led Real Sociedad to three league wins, defeating Deportivo La Coruna 3-2, Malaga 5-2 and Levante 2-1. Despite their strong performances, Mourinho secured the recognition after Madrid’s perfect league record and victory over their arch-rivals. The award marks another milestone in the Portuguese manager’s return to the Santiago Bernabeu, where he previously coached from 2010 to 2013. During his first spell, Mourinho won the La Liga title, Copa del Rey and Spanish Super Cup. He succeeds Barcelona manager Hansi Flick, who won the September award. Madrid have also maintained a strong position in the title race, sitting second in the standings, three points behind Barcelona. They have suffered two league defeats this season, against Real Betis and Atletico Madrid. nigeria.title: Brighton’s Yohanna makes Chelle’s 23-man list for DR Congo clash
nigeria.description: Brighton forward Zadok Yohanna and Molde FC midfielder Daniel Daga have been named in Nigeria’s 23-man squad for the 2028 Olympic Games football qualifiers against the Democratic Republic of Congo. nigeria.title: Yari never called Nigerian youths lazy – Group insists
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Senator Yari National Unity Project for Tinubu 2027 has dismissed reports that Senator Abdul’aziz Abubakar Yari described Nigerian youths as lazy, accusing sections of the media of misrepresenting his remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State. The group said Yari, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, was speaking about hunger, food availability and the dignity of hard work, rather than disparaging young Nigerians. In a statement issued by its National Coordinator, Dr Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, the group challenged those circulating the allegation to watch the full footage of Yari’s address, insisting that the senator had acknowledged the economic hardship facing Nigerians before making his remarks on productivity. “He opened his remark by stating plainly: ‘We have hunger.’ At no point in that remark did the Senator mention, single out or describe Nigerian youths. To turn a statement on the dignity of work, made by a man who had just acknowledged that hunger exists, into the headline ‘Yari calls youths lazy’ is not reporting; it is spin,” the statement said. To support its position, the group cited Yari’s interventions in education, military recruitment, agriculture and public-sector employment, arguing that his record demonstrated his commitment to the welfare and empowerment of young Nigerians. It also claimed that Yari facilitated the enlistment of 158 young people from Zamfara West into two Nigerian Army recruitment intakes and supported farmers with agricultural inputs and equipment. “A leader who sends thousands of young people to university and into national service does not hold Nigerian youths in contempt; he invests in them,” the statement added. The group reaffirmed its confidence in Yari and directed its officers nationwide to intensify grassroots mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. It also urged media organisations that published the disputed report to review the full footage of the senator’s address and correct what it described as a misrepresentation. “Political disagreement is legitimate; misrepresentation is not,” the statement added. nigeria.title: ICPC files amended charge against Adeyemi, adds four civil servants
nigeria.description: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has filed amended charges against Adeniyi Adeyemi, the purported director general of the non-existent Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council (PFIPC). The prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, told the court that ICPC expanded the previous 22 counts to 36. Tahir said that the four suspects are Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe and included in the new charge. The case was originally filed by the Nigerian police. Monday’s proceedings, which originally slated for hearing of Adeyemi’s bail application, was halted because of the charge amendment, requiring all defendants, including Adeyemi, to enter their pleas. However, the plea taking could not proceed because the fourth defendant, Omameh, was absent from court on health grounds. The rest of the defendants were in court. ”Her unavailability in court has constrained the prosecution from proceeding with the arraignment, this being a criminal charge,” Tahir said. He relied on Section 266 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) for his application. Tahir argued that an accused person has to be present in court throughout the trial, “subject to the exception stated therein.” He, therefore, urged the court for a short adjournment to allow the fourth defendant time to recover and enter her plea. Adeyemi’s counsel, Ibrahim Angulu, SAN, did not object to the amended charge or adjournment. However, he reminded the court of Adeyemi’s prolonged detention. Meanwhile, Justice Yusuf Halilu adjourned until Nov. 18 for the arraignment of the suspects. He, however, ordered that Adeyemi should be taken back to Kuje Correctional Facility and the other defendants to return to the ICPC detention facility. nigeria.description: Nigeria made an impressive start to the athletics competition at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday, winning gold in both the men’s and women’s 100m finals at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop. Rosemary Nwankwo opened the country’s gold-medal account in the women’s 100m, crossing the finish line in 11.16 seconds to claim victory and set a new personal best. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) Nigeria’s celebrations continued minutes later as Gift Bright secured another gold medal in the men’s 100m, finishing in a personal-best time of 10.28 seconds. China’s Zhang Hangyu came second in 10.57 seconds, while Poland’s Szymon Dolega claimed bronze in 10.61 seconds. nigeria.title: Obi Alleges NFF Blocked Him From Greeting Victorious Flamingos
nigeria.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi has alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) prevented him from greeting members of the national Under-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Obi said he was allegedly informed that the officials had warned against allowing him to approach the players, allegedly threatening that they would lose their jobs if he did. The former Anambra State governor disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X handle on Monday, after the Flamingos returned to Nigeria following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Morocco. Obi said he arrived at the airport at about 7 a.m. on Monday to board a flight to Enugu when he sighted the victorious team preparing to leave the airport. Flamingos arriving in Nigeria. He said he subsequently asked his protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could greet and welcome the players. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my Protocol Officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation (NFF) had refused and had requested that I not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs,” he wrote. Obi described the incident as another example of what he called the growing culture of “toxic politics” in Nigeria, alleging that he had experienced similar treatment during a previous visit to a football event. He recounted that on March 25, 2025, he travelled to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for a World Cup qualifying match, where he said the governor received him at the VIP stand. According to him, after the match, other government officials were allowed to greet the players, but he was again prevented from doing so. “Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. The former governor expressed concern over what he described as the increasing politicisation of public engagements, arguing that political differences should not prevent Nigerians from celebrating national achievements. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. nigeria.title: PFIPC Scandal: FG Files Fresh Amended Charges Against Adeyemi Adeniyi, Four Others
nigeria.description: The Federal Government has filed a fresh 36-count amended charge against the embattled Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Adeyemi Adeniyi, and four others over alleged forgery, false representation and fraud. Adeniyi appeared alongside his co-defendants before Justice Halilu Yusuf of the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Monday. However, their arraignment on the fresh charges could not proceed due to the absence of the fourth defendant, Florence Omemah, who was reportedly ill. Prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, informed the court that Ms Omemah was receiving treatment at a hospital in Abuja. He subsequently requested a seven-day adjournment to enable her to recover and appear in court to take her plea. Counsel to Mr Adeniyi, Ibrahim Angulu, however, urged the court to grant a shorter adjournment to allow him to pursue bail for his client. He also told the court that Mr Adeniyi had been in detention for more than 200 days. In a brief ruling, Justice Yusuf adjourned the case until November 18 for the arraignment of all the defendants. The judge further ordered that Mr Adeniyi be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre, while the other defendants should remain in the custody of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). Alleged Fake Government Agency Adeniyi Adeyemi paraded himself as the DG of the PFIPC. Photo: X@BayoOnanuga. The case centres on allegations that Adeniyi established a fictitious federal agency known as the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council and falsely presented himself as its director-general. Investigators alleged that the agency had no legal backing and that Mr Adeniyi forged appointment letters and signatures attributed to the Chief of Staff to the President to legitimise his purported position. According to investigators, he occupied offices previously used by the defunct Presidential Economic Advisory Council at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja and allegedly held unauthorised meetings with foreign diplomats. He was also accused of seeking official visa documentation for United States visas and operating 34 bank accounts. Investigators further alleged that he exploited loopholes in the civil service system to secure a proposed allocation of ₦1.302 billion for the fictitious agency in the 2026 budget. ICPC Uncovers Other Alleged Fake Agencies Following an interim report presented to President Bola Tinubu, the ICPC reportedly uncovered two other allegedly fictitious agencies linked to Mr Adeniyi: the FCT Investment Promotion Agency and the Foreign Investment Promotion Agency. The commission also recommended disciplinary action against some public officials suspected of assisting the alleged scheme. A Binance spokesperson confirmed to CoinDesk the closure date over the weekend, saying the exchange is “progressively restricting certain services for affected users” now that the transition period under the Markets in Crypto-Assets framework has ended. “Affected accounts will be closed with effect from 31 December 2026,” the spokesperson said, calling it “a carefully managed process.” Binance said customer assets remain safe and accessible and described the move as “no sudden freeze.” Deposits are already blocked, but users can still withdraw crypto and fiat. Accounts holding less than the fee would lose the entire balance, the emails say. Anyone who withdraws everything before Nov. 29 pays nothing. business.title: U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have formally withdrawn a 2020 proposal that would have cut the Bank Secrecy Act threshold for cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, leaving the existing $3,000 line in place. The notice, published Monday in the Federal Register, says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Fed’s Board of Governors “will not take further action” on a proposal they first issued on Oct. 27, 2020. That plan would have lowered the recordkeeping and Travel Rule thresholds to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. Those rules require banks and nonbank financial institutions to collect, retain and pass along customer information on transfers of $3,000 or more. It also would have clarified the meaning of “money” in both rules so they apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency, along with digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. Why the agencies backed off Per the notcie, FinCEN and the Fed received nearly 3,000 comments on the proposal, most of them substantially similar form letters. Commenters generally opposed the lower threshold, arguing that it would burden smaller institutions and could push consumers sending remittances toward less regulated channels. Many also noted that potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already being flagged to FinCEN through suspicious activity reports. Several said the threshold should rise instead, citing inflation since 1995. Sentiment on the crypto language was mixed. Companies that provide crypto services and their trade groups opposed it, citing technical limits and the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transfers, while some banks and money services businesses supported it. The agencies gave two reasons for pulling the proposal. More than five years have passed, and they said more public feedback would help before adopting anything similar. The withdrawal, they wrote, gives the public “certainty” that no final rule will be issued without another chance to comment. The second reason is the crypto industry itself. The notice says crypto markets “have continued to mature” and new legal frameworks are emerging, citing the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted on July 18, 2025. Any future change tied to crypto, the agencies said, should be considered in light of those developments so it is “fit for purpose.” What the withdrawal does and does not do The notice does not repeal or amend any rule. The $3,000 threshold that has applied for decades stays where it is, and so does the existing Travel Rule. What disappears is the specific path to $250 and the proposed wording that would have written crypto into the definition of money. The agencies did not say whether they plan a new proposal or offer a timeline. The withdrawal is the latest in a run of reversals from Treasury. On Oct.

business.title: Coinbase Wins Full Federal Trust Charter From OCC
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Wins Full Federal Trust Charter From OCC Coinbase has won a full national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, upgrading the conditional approval it received in April and putting its institutional custody business under direct federal supervision, the exchange said Monday. The OCC approved the application for Coinbase National Trust Company last Friday, the company said in a blog post. OCC licensing records, as reported, show the chartering process was completed Nov. 6. Coinbase applied in October 2025 and received preliminary approval on April 2. In the intervening months it had to finish its organizational and operational preparations before the OCC would let the trust bank open. “This charter allows us to bring clear and consistent federal uniformity to our industry-leading custody capabilities,” Coinbase wrote, adding that it strengthens the regulatory framework under which it serves customers. The company said it has served as a custodian for more than 14 years. What the charter allows A national trust bank can hold assets for clients as a fiduciary, and Coinbase’s focus is custody for institutional customers. It is not a commercial bank. It cannot take ordinary retail deposits or make loans, and the charter does not authorize it to issue stablecoins. Staking, prime trading and financing will keep running through Coinbase affiliates, not the trust itself. Under the OCC’s April decision, the trust bank acts as an intermediary for those services and does not perform them directly. The decision also sets conditions. The trust bank must hold at least $60 million in Tier 1 capital and enough liquid assets to cover 180 days of operating expenses during its first three years. The license does not automatically connect Coinbase to Federal Reserve payment systems either. That requires a separate application under the Fed’s account access guidelines. Coinbase already runs custody through Coinbase Custody Trust Company, a limited-purpose trust regulated by the New York State Department of Financial Services. The company plans to move that business to the national entity over three years. A crowded charter queue Coinbase is the latest crypto firm to complete a federal trust charter. Ripple received final approval on Oct. 26, and Circle won final OCC approval in July, a decision that put USDC reserves on a path toward federal supervision. The OCC has been courting the sector. In August, Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould said “America and the OCC are once again open for business,” as the regulator touted its charter push. Ripple, Circle, Crypto.com and Paxos had all received conditional approval by then. Block applied for its own banking charter in September. The approval did not come without resistance. Nvidia probe and Iran stall hit weekend trading Crypto was the only major market open when two headlines landed. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. Wealthy people do not always look wealthy. Some of the most financially secure people I have met do not drive the loudest cars. And some of the people who look the richest are one bad month away from panic. entertainment.description: Toyin Abraham’s directorial comedy drama Oversabi Aunty is now streaming on Netflix and Kava. Nigerian cinema has witnessed an unprecedented commercial evolution over recent years, with local box office totals soaring past figures once considered unthinkable. From the era when a four-hundred-million-Naira milestone set the nationwide ceiling to an era defined by multi-billion-Naira theatrical runs, audiences across West Africa continue to show up in massive numbers for homegrown storytelling. Here is a look at the five highest-grossing Nollywood blockbusters in history that have continually redefined theatrical success, shattered industry records, and set historic commercial benchmarks across Nigerian cinemas. Directed by Funke Akindele and Tobi Makinde for the Funke Ayotunde Akindele Network (FAAN), the story follows Jedidah Judah—played by Akindele herself—and her five sons from different fathers as they scheme to rob a luxury furniture shop to fund their mother’s life-saving medical care. entertainment.title: How Seyi Ademeso Turned Awkwardness Into the Meshkiey Brand
entertainment.description: Some people spend years trying to avoid awkward situations. Seyi Ademeso has built a career out of creating them, in the identity of Meshkiey . The content creator has turned everyday social discomfort into a distinctive style of comedy, earning an audience that recognises him for his unconventional approach to skits. But there is more to Seyi than the character who seems willing to embarrass himself for a laugh. Beyond the camera, he is a creative strategist, entrepreneur and businessman with ambitions that stretch far beyond social media. In this exclusive, we sat down with him to talk about the journey, the person behind the persona and what he hopes to build next. Hello Meshkiey. How are you feeling today? I’m feeling good. Honestly, I’m grateful. I’m excited to have this conversation and reflect on the journey. Before Meshkiey became the person people know online, what were you like growing up? I think I’ve always been a very observant person. Even growing up, I noticed little things about people, the way they behaved, the way they spoke, the funny things people did without realising they were funny. I was also quite expressive. I wouldn’t necessarily say I was the loudest person in every room, but I definitely had a personality. I liked making people laugh, and I enjoyed doing things differently. Looking back, I think a lot of the things people now associate with Meshkiey were actually already there. The difference is that I eventually found a platform where I could turn those traits into something creative. When did you start creating, really? I started creating around 2016, and honestly, there wasn’t some grand master plan behind it. I think I just wanted to create. I had a phone, I had ideas, and I was fascinated by what people were doing online. At the time, content creation wasn’t necessarily viewed as a serious career path the way it is today. My early content was very different from what people know me for now. I was experimenting a lot, trying different formats and figuring out what felt natural to me. I didn’t have the polished understanding of branding or storytelling that I have today. I was basically learning in public. I was creating, posting, seeing what people responded to and slowly discovering my voice. entertainment.title: “When Are You Coming Home?” ValueJet Restores Daily Flights to Asaba Ahead of the Festive Season
entertainment.description: Daily Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja services resume on Friday, 20 November 2026, strengthening regional connectivity and bringing families together for the holidays. Somewhere in Lagos or Abuja right now, a phone is ringing, and the voice on the other end is asking the single question that marks the true beginning of the Nigerian festive season: “When are you coming home?” For thousands of professionals, business owners, and families whose answer is Asaba and the surrounding communities across Delta and Anambra states, ValueJet has delivered timely news. The airline will officially resume daily scheduled flights on its Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja routes starting Friday, 20 November 2026, just as year-end travel planning reaches peak momentum. The end of the year carries an undeniable emotional pull back to one’s roots. It is the season of growing gift lists, overpacked suitcases, group chats buzzing with reunion itineraries, and the quiet warmth of returning to familiar streets. For many families, December represents the single period in the year when loved ones assemble under one roof. By reintroducing daily non-stop frequency on both routes, ValueJet provides critical operational flexibility for holiday travelers. Whether passengers are heading home early to spend the entire season with family or flying out closer to Christmas Eve after wrapping up the work year, the restored schedule ensures seamless travel options tailored to diverse holiday schedules. “The festive season is fundamentally about people, relationships, and shared moments. At ValueJet, our mission is to ensure that distance never stands in the way of those connections,” said Omololu Majekodunmi , Managing Director of ValueJet. “Restoring our daily services to Asaba reflects our deep commitment to serving the travel needs of our passengers during the most important time of the year. We are proud to offer a reliable, comfortable, and affordable gateway home for families and communities across the region.” The Lagos–Asaba service bridges Nigeria’s commercial capital directly with the vibrant heart of Delta State, facilitating easy access across the South-South and South-East regions. Simultaneously, the Asaba–Abuja route delivers a direct, hassle-free link between the nation’s capital and Asaba, eliminating lengthy road journeys and complex connection itineraries. The resumption complements ValueJet’s rapidly expanding domestic and regional network. Domestically, the airline provides essential air links to key destinations including Port Harcourt, Jos, Owerri, Calabar, Benin, and GWI-Iperu. Beyond Nigeria’s borders, ValueJet continues to extend its reach beyond established destinations like Accra, Banjul, Cotonou, and Malabo with upcoming regional route expansions to Libreville, Monrovia, and Abidjan. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. SHOW AND AVAILABILITY Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. sports.title: ‘He’s a coward. He can’t coach’: Dave Portnoy demands apology after being ‘right about Ryan Day from the jump’
sports.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect It was a rough weekend for Michigan, as the Wolverines lost to rival Michigan State and fired their offensive coordinator. But Barstool Sports founder and devoted Michigan fan Dave Portnoy still found something to celebrate. Ohio State suffered a blowout loss of its own, falling to Oregon for its second straight defeat. And Portnoy, who has been a longtime critic of Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day, said he’s owed an apology from every Ohio State fan in Columbus. Portnoy’s Feud With Ryan Day Portnoy has been one of Day’s harshest critics for years, and things have only gotten more personal this season. In August, he called Day a “scared little chicken-boy” after Ohio State moved its senior day from the Michigan game to Week 1. Then in October, Barstool was removed from Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff , and Portnoy blamed Day for the decision. “I always knew Ryan Day was soft but holy sh*t even I didnt realize he was this soft,” Portnoy wrote on X at the time, calling the Buckeyes coach “Cryin Ryan.” Awful Announcing noted that the breakup was always inevitable . A couple of weeks later, Portnoy said that Day “would be unsuccessful at any program other than Ohio State.” “Ryan Day was born on third base,” Portnoy said. “Like, anybody here could coach that team to 10, 11 wins.” This weekend gave Portnoy plenty of new material. Michigan fell 15-6 to Michigan State, and the Wolverines fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, whom Portnoy had called “horrific.” But Ohio State blew a 14-0 lead in a 41-28 loss to Oregon, its second straight defeat, and Day said afterward that “there needs to be accountability” for the team’s struggles. ‘He’s a coward’ On Monday’s episode of Wake Up Barstool , Portnoy made it clear that he was enjoying Ohio State’s struggles. “I want an apology from every single person in Columbus. I want them to get in line and line up,” Portnoy said, in a clip shared by the show . “I want them all to come in a receiving line and say, ‘Hey, Dave Portnoy, you’ve been right about Ryan Day from the jump. He’s a coward. He can’t coach. He was born on third base.’ All of it. Get in line and say, ‘I’m sorry, you should be back on Big Noon Kickoff . It was a joke what they did to you,'” he continued. Portnoy admitted that Michigan has problems of its own, but he said that Ohio State’s situation is even worse given the talent on the roster. “Yes, we have problems in Ann Arbor, but that team’s a joke with the talent they have. So yeah, real bad weekend for Michigan, no doubt,” Portnoy said. “But let’s not forget, as bad as a weekend Michigan had, Michigan State had a worse weekend, and Ohio State had the worst weekend of the bunch.” Needless to say, Portnoy is going to enjoy every minute of this before The Game. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson) (Brynn Anderson/Associated Press) The Jacksonville Jaguars took a big swing a day before the NFL trade deadline , grabbing All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons on Monday morning, according to multiple reports . The Jaguars (6-2), who are just a half-game behind the Buffalo Bills and Denver Broncos for best record in the AFC and have a three-game lead over the Houston Texans in the AFC South, are giving up a second-round pick in next year's NFL draft and a fifth-rounder in 2028. By comparison, the Texans gave up a second- and seventh-rounder in exchange for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and a sixth-round pick last month. Bates, who will turn 30 years old in February, is in the final year of a four-year, $64 million contract and is still playing well. The former second-round pick out of Wake Forest, made the Pro Bowl in 2023 and was second-team All-Pro last season. Bates, who has made 61 straight starts and hasn't missed a game since 2022, also was second-team All-Pro in 2020 and 2023. "Woke up a Jaguar!," Bates posted on Twitter on Monday morning. The Jaguars had an urgent need at safety ever since former Texans defensive back Eric Murray was lost for the season due to an elbow he injury he suffered against the Colts last week. Murray, who left the Texans for a three-year, $19.5 million contract with Jacksonville following the 2024 season, had started 17 games for the Jaguars over the past two seasons before the injury. The Jaguars' defense ranks second in the league, giving up just 15.1 points per game, but they have been vulnerable through the air. Jacksonville ranks 22nd in pass defense, allowing 229 passing yards per game. When the Texans beat Jacksonville 34-31 in London last month, C.J. Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns. sports.title: Mowbray's 'soldiers and artists' march up the table
sports.description: [BBC] Since the lengthy international break across September and October, Blackburn Rovers have taken 12 points from a possible 21. That is a healthy return by any measure. The only real blemish was the 4-0 hammering at Swansea City , a day on which Rovers never turned up. Beyond that, there has been plenty to like. With just over a third of the season gone, it feels like the perfect moment to take stock. Most importantly, Rovers are looking up, not down. Twelve months ago, supporters were nervously checking the bottom end of the table. Now the conversation is about the play-offs. That alone tells you how much has changed. And it's about more than points. Ewood Park feels alive again. That revival began under Michael O'Neill, but Tony Mowbray has kept the momentum going. Matchdays feel like events once more. The big away followings have helped. Not many clubs can hand over more than 7,000 tickets to travelling supporters, and fans have responded in numbers. Crowds nudging 20,000 for games against Middlesbrough, Coventry City, Leicester City and West Ham over the past seven months have brought a buzz back to the place. The only defeat among them came in a dead-rubber against an already relegated Leicester side. The positivity extends beyond the stands. Most of this squad bears the scars of last season's struggles. Apart from Sam Morsy, Jayden Fevrier and Gady Beyuku, these players have lived through difficult times at Ewood. Yet they look liberated rather than burdened by the experience. That's where the Mowbray factor comes in. His "soldiers and artists" philosophy sounds simple, but right now it's working a treat. The artists are thriving. Todd Cantwell and Dapo Afolayan have become central figures. Both have stayed fit. Both along with centre back Sean McLoughlin are ever-presents. Both are proving they can be difference-makers. That's a far cry from last season. Afolayan managed just one start after his February arrival and was hooked at half-time. Cantwell started fewer than half of Rovers' league games and never really had the freedom to express himself. This team is playing with far more adventure, which suits both players perfectly. Anyone familiar with Mowbray's career should not be surprised. For all his reputation as a no-nonsense centre-half, his teams have always tried to attack. That's in his DNA. It always has been. Then there are the soldiers. Morsy remains the heartbeat of the side. Mowbray calls him his coach on the pitch and it is easy to understand why. His influence seems to be rubbing off on academy graduate Kristi Montgomery, who looks increasingly comfortable at Championship level. Together, they give Rovers a solid foundation. If they trade Baker, the trade of Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars , involving a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, is a good benchmark to hit. The Cardinals might be able to get more for Baker. That is, if they even trade him. A Baker trade is a huge hurdle to clear, and even if teams make strong offers, Arizona might decide to keep Baker. That would put Miami in the top two positions of the next NFL draft, which is helpful, considering Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith and Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker may be the top two picks. sports.title: 'My will is to stay' - Alisson Becker opens up on Liverpool contract future and desire for new deal
sports.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker has broken his silence regarding his long-term future at Anfield, expressing a clear desire to extend his stay on Merseyside. The Brazilian international, whose current deal is approaching its conclusion, remains a pivotal figure for the Reds as they navigate a new era under the current coaching staff. Alisson confirms desire for Anfield extension Speaking about his current mindset regarding a potential contract renewal, in quotes reported by BBC Sport , Alisson was incredibly transparent about where he sees himself playing in the coming years. 'Yes [I want to stay], in my mind. I'm focused on playing every game but in my mind I'm happy to stay,' said Alisson. The 34-year-old goalkeeper, who made a £66.8m switch from Roma in 2018 and has since amassed 347 appearances for the Reds, remains a fundamental figure at Anfield . The Brazilian further elaborated on the factors that will influence his final decision, though his personal preference is already set in stone. 'That depends on a lot of aspects and different situations. But my will is to stay - I'm happy here and my family is happy here,' he explained. 'I'm still hungry for titles and delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can, so that's my thinking.' Contract negotiations and managerial backing When asked directly if he had engaged in formal talks over a new contract, the keeper clarified the current status of the situation. 'No, but my agent is talking with the club,' he revealed. The Brazilian has established a legendary status at Anfield, having won two Premier League titles, two League Cups, the FA Cup, the Champions League, and the Club World Cup during his time with the club. The goalkeeper's desire to stay aligns perfectly with the public stance taken by the Liverpool coaching staff. Last week, head coach Andoni Iraola addressed the uncertainty surrounding the veteran, admitting he was unsure if this would be the final chapter for the Brazilian but expressing a strong wish for him to remain part of the project. Iraola noted that he hoped the goalkeeper could 'continue for more time,' recognizing the immense value Alisson brings not just in terms of shot-stopping, but also in his leadership within the dressing room. Building consistency for a title charge Following a difficult week that saw Liverpool suffer setbacks against Arsenal and Fenerbahce, Alisson produced a series of crucial saves to help secure a vital victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday. However, for Alisson, individual brilliance is not enough; he believes the squad must find a higher level of collective stability if they are to return to the summit of English and European football. 'Our reality is that we're not doing as well as we can. It doesn't mean that we are not doing well - we are doing well in so many games - but the consistency is not there yet,' he admitted.

The 19-year-old FC Barcelona centre-back has been named the winner of the 2026 Golden Boy award, presented annually by Italian newspaper Tuttosport since 2003 to recognise the most outstanding footballer under 21 playing in Europe’s leagues. The decision was officially announced early on Monday afternoon at a formal ceremony in the Italian town of Sassuolo. A milestone for defenders Cubarsí’s triumph marks a rare milestone in the award’s history: he is only the second centre-back to receive the honour in its more than two decades of existence, following in the footsteps of Dutchman Matthijs de Ligt in 2018. The roll of honour has otherwise traditionally been reserved for renowned forwards and playmakers such as Lionel Messi, Wayne Rooney, Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham. Barça dominance and Spanish representation With this trophy, FC Barcelona extends its record at the top of the award’s all-time standings. Cubarsí joins Lionel Messi, Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal as the five La Masia-trained players to have claimed the Golden Boy while wearing Barça’s colours. Cubarsí succeeds Désiré Doué (2025) and Lamine Yamal (2024), reaffirming Spanish football’s prominence in an edition whose nominees also included Jon Martín (Real Sociedad) and his teammates Marc Bernal and Xavi Espart. Discussing reports linking Frimpong with Saudi Arabia on Anfield Index’s Media Matters podcast, Lynch argued that positional difficulties and injury problems had combined to make the signing unsuccessful so far. He went as far as predicting that the Netherlands international could leave before next season. That was his assessment of the situation, rather than confirmation of an agreed transfer or an active negotiation. technology.description: NASA is moving ahead with its plan to repurpose a Mars rover engineering model as a lunar trundlebot for less than $400 million. The robot, dubbed PROMISE (Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration), is a cut-and-shut of engineering test articles used for the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers, currently rolling around the Red Planet. During a weekend briefing , NASA outlined the plan for PROMISE: to land the robot on the lunar surface by late 2028 for an 18-month mission. PROMISE will be preceded by NASA's VIPER trundlebot, which is expected to survive only 100 days on the Moon's surface. PROMISE will carry copies of VIPER's science instruments, including a drill capable of boring 1 meter into the lunar regolith. Power will come from a Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG) left over from the Cassini mission. NASA acknowledged the fuel was processed some time ago – the Cassini mission to Saturn was launched in 1997 – but anticipates there will be plenty of heat and power for PROMISE's components. Blue Origin is to deposit the rover on the Moon. NASA awarded the company a $94 million base contract, "with an option period worth an additional $140 million based on performance to deliver PROMISE to the lunar South Pole." The figures make it difficult to ascertain the exact cost of the PROMISE mission. However, during the briefing, NASA said it had "a pretty firm agreement with JPL to basically deliver the rover to the surface under $400 million." The $400 million includes the lander, which will be Blue Origin's Mark 1. Earlier this year, The Planetary Society's chief of space policy, Casey Drier, estimated that the mission (including repurposing the hardware developed for Mars and landing it on the Moon) would cost at least $723 million. At the time, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said: "if PROMISE costs even 20 percent of your low-end estimate, we simply will not fly it." Assuming Isaacman was only talking about the rover, Drier's figure drops to $489 million without launch and landing costs. 20 percent of that is… not going to be enough. That also doesn't account for the impact of taking away the hardware built for the Mars program. During the briefing, NASA said it was "pretty comfortable" with how the Mars rovers were going and so was happy about repurposing the hardware or, as one speaker put it, "can we give it a new paint job?" A source told The Register that morale at the agency's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) was not high at present. Raiding successful programs to fulfill the administration's whims is unlikely to have improved the mood of engineers. Still. Another trundlebot on the Moon. Far better than using that spare RTG for yet another deep space mission, right? ®

technology.title: Microsoft's Azure Linux gets 470-plus security fixes in one almighty patching session
technology.description: Microsoft has unleashed a whopper of an update for Azure Linux, packing more than 470 CVE fixes into a single release as the software industry's ever-growing pile of vulnerabilities shows little sign of shrinking. Over the weekend, Microsoft rolled out Azure Linux 3.0.2022 with fixes covering everything from the Linux kernel to open source packages and container software. The changelog runs to hundreds of entries, so anyone planning to read the whole thing might want to put the kettle on. Microsoft's release notes contain more than 470 CVE references, although some vulnerabilities appear multiple times because they affect different packages. So that's not necessarily 470 separate security holes, but it's still an impressive amount of patching for one release. The fixes span OpenSSL, curl, Kubernetes, Docker, QEMU, and a lengthy list of other packages that underpin modern Linux environments. The generic Linux kernel has been updated to version 6.6.161.1. There's also been some housekeeping following the eMudhra certificate incident , tracked as CVE-2026-114406. Microsoft has removed or distrusted root certificates that could validate compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates, while adding checks in Python and Go to reject the affected certificates. It has also preserved SSL.com TLS trust where required, presumably to avoid fixing one certificate headache by creating another. Container infrastructure gets plenty of attention, too, with fixes spanning KubeVirt, containerd, Docker Compose, and other components used to keep cloud workloads running. Several CVEs crop up repeatedly across these packages, helping explain the eye-watering number of entries in the changelog. The release includes less security-focused changes too, including new Dockerfiles, an OpenVMM patch for confidential computing support, fixes for systemd hangs, and adjustments to GRUB Secure Boot metadata. The hefty release comes amid an AI-fueled surge in vulnerability discovery that has left developers struggling to keep up with the resulting patch workload. As The Register reported e arlier today, Linux creator Linus Torvalds reckons there may finally be signs that the flood is easing, at least in some corners of the kernel. Torvalds said fixes are now arriving faster than new bug reports in the kernel's eBPF subsystem, although he noted that most other areas haven't reached that point. Whether the wider software industry is anywhere close to catching up is another matter, and Microsoft hasn't said if AI-assisted research contributed to the vulnerabilities addressed in this release. Azure Linux, formerly known as CBL-Mariner, is Microsoft's own Linux distribution, developed primarily for its cloud infrastructure and services. That makes keeping its many components patched rather more important than the modest version-number bump might suggest. And judging by the size of this latest changelog, Microsoft's patching teams aren't likely to be putting their feet up anytime soon. ®
